title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the study of the 'cyclotomic map' X_n inside the theory of maps (cartes, later called dessins d'enfants).

**Setup from the previous page.** X_n is the n-gon map on P^1(C):
- vertices: the n-th roots of unity μ_n;
- edges: the arcs of the unit circle joining them;
- faces: two n-gons, with centres 0 and ∞.

It is the pull-back of the 'universal map' X_0 = ({0} ⊂ [0,1] ⊂ P^1) under g_n(z) = −(z^n−1)²/(4z^n). This g_n is a Belyi map of degree 2n and is Galois with dihedral group D_n of order 2n. Its fibres are:
- over 0: z^n = 1, the vertices, with index 2;
- over 1: z^n = −1, the edge midpoints, with index 2;
- over ∞: z = 0 and z = ∞, the face centres, with index n.

X_n^* is X_n with the vertices removed. It is a Galois branched cover of X_0^* = X_0∖{0}, branched only over 1 and ∞ with indices 2 and n.

**Formula (93).** The 'general theory of mixed fundamental groups' (equivariant fundamental groups of a space with a finite group action) and of 'fundamental groups with signature' (orbifold fundamental groups) gives a canonical isomorphism, defined only up to inner automorphism. It runs from the D_n-equivariant fundamental group of X_n^* to the orbifold fundamental group of P^1 with signature ∞·{0} + 2·{1} + n·{∞}. That group is Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1², ρ_∞^n⟩ ≅ Z/2 * Z/n, i.e. a modular-type triangle group (2, n, ∞).

**Fixing the base points.** To make the isomorphism exact rather than outer, the base point must be moved. The natural one, P_{n+} = 0 (a face centre), maps to ∞, a branch point. So it must be replaced by a point lying over U_{0,3} = P^1∖{0,1,∞}.

Grothendieck uses the barycentric subdivision for this:
- X_0 splits into the two hemispheres X_0^±, the upper and lower half-planes.
- Their preimages are the 4n triangles ('flags', or 'repères') of the barycentric subdivision of X_n.
- The 2n direct flags correspond to the 2n flags of the polygon P, i.e. to the elements of D_n acting simply transitively.

The rigidification (épinglage) of P singles out an origin flag r_0 = (vertex R_0, edge midpoint Q_{a0}, face centre P_ω). It maps biholomorphically onto X_0^+ with R_0 ↦ 0, Q_{a0} ↦ 1, P_ω ↦ ∞.

The base point is taken to be the point P ∈ r_0 lying over the 'north pole' P_+ = e^{iπ/3} of X_0^+. This point is the fixed point of the order-3 symmetry z ↦ 1/(1−z), i.e. the barycentre of the upper triangle.

**What this serves.** The next page uses these choices to write an explicit (non-outer) homomorphism (ℓ, g) ↦ g_n(ℓ). It then computes the images of the generators ρ and σ_{a0} of the cartographic group in Z/2 * Z/n. This makes the identification of the oriented map's automorphism data with the quotient of Π_{0,3} explicit: a dictionary between rigidified maps and finite-index subgroups / Π_{0,3}-sets.
errors: As written on this page, (93) asserts an isomorphism from the ordinary fundamental group π_1(X_n^*) to the orbifold group π_1(X_0, ∞{0}+2{1}+n{∞}). This is false: π_1 of the cover is only an index-2n normal subgroup, with quotient D_n. The left side must be the D_n-equivariant ('mixed') fundamental group π_1(X_n^*, D_n; P), as Grothendieck himself corrects in (95)–(97) on the next page by inserting 'D_n;'.

Minor: the count '4n repères' is overwritten as '2n drapeaux'. In fact the barycentric subdivision has 4n flags/triangles, of which 2n are direct, so both figures appear correctly in the final sentence; the correction is only terminological.

ideas.what: Cyclotomic (regular n-gon) map X_n realised by the explicit dihedral Belyi map g_n(z) = −(z^n−1)²/(4z^n) onto the universal map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse 1984); Jones–Singerman, Wolfart for regular maps and dessins
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions maps and Belyi; this explicit formula is not quoted there to my knowledge

ideas.what: Isomorphism between the equivariant ('mixed') fundamental group of a Galois branched cover and the orbifold fundamental group with signature of the base, Π_{0,3}/⟨ρ_1², ρ_∞^n⟩
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group; π_1 of a quotient stack [X/G]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds); classical Fuchsian group theory; SGA1 tame fundamental group
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (tame/log ramification); Esquisse alludes to fundamental groups of multiplicity-weighted curves

ideas.what: Fixing base points canonically via the origin flag of the barycentric subdivision, with the base point P_+ = e^{iπ/3} at the S_3-symmetric barycentre of the upper half-plane, so that outer isomorphisms become genuine ones
ideas.modern_name: base point choice for Π_{0,3}; compare tangential base points (Deligne, Ihara) and the symmetric point ρ = e^{iπ/3}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (1989) for tangential base points; Ihara for Galois action on Π_{0,3}

missed.claim: Grothendieck uses the symmetric point e^{iπ/3} inside the upper half-plane, i.e. the barycentre of the origin flag, as base point to rigidify the isomorphisms for rigidified (épinglées) maps. The later standard is tangential base points at 0. This is a minor alternative convention compatible with the S_3 symmetry; it is not a new result.
missed.quote: Prenons le point P∈r_0 qui s'envoie sur le "pôle nord" P_+ (=exp 2iπ/6) ∈ X_0^+
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it documents an S_3-symmetric base-point convention for the dessin/Π_{0,3} dictionary predating Deligne's tangential base points.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful worked example of standard material: dihedral Belyi map, orbifold π_1 ≅ Z/2*Z/n, and base-point bookkeeping via flags of the barycentric subdivision. The symmetric base-point choice is a nice detail but not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: 'subdivision barycentrique de la sorte X_n' should read 'de la carte X_n'.
In (93) the left side is written π_1(X_n^*, P_{n+}) with P_{n+} = 0 under it; the 'D_n;' is only added on the next page.
In the right-hand figure, γ (dashed path from P_+) and g_n(α_ρ) are path labels, and 0, 1 mark the segment [0,1] on the equator.
